channel.title: Security Advisories on Grafana Labs
channel.description: Recent content in Security Advisories on Grafana Labs

item.title: Strava datasource can be used to access arbitrary resource
item.description: The Strava datasource plugin’s /strava-api resource handler forwarded a client-supplied endpoint to the Strava API without validation. Any user with the datasources:query permission (Viewers by default) could read any Strava API path allowed by the connected account’s OAuth grant. Requests are GET only, so the issue is read-only. Affected: plugin versions 1.2.0 through 1.7.2. Fixed in 1.7.3, which restricts the endpoint to the five paths the plugin uses and validates it before the access token is resolved.

item.title: Authorization bypass in the Git Sync provisioning jobs API
item.description:
A user with the Editor role could delete, move, push or pull Git Sync managed resources in folders where they only had view access, by creating a provisioning job through the jobs resource API, which skipped the folder permission checks (incorrect authorization).

Thanks to igzs2 for reporting this vulnerability to us via our bug bounty program.

item.title: Alerting contact point authorization bypass via schema downgrade
item.description: A user with permission to edit contact points but not their protected fields can change protected settings, such as a contact point’s destination URL, by switching an integration to a legacy schema version, which can expose stored credentials and redirect alert notifications (incorrect authorization).
